correctness.rationale: An arbitrary nonzero periodic word must contain zero. Rotation fixes the last symbol at zero; the binary nonzero indicator must have weight divisible by three, and it determines the word uniquely by exact partial sums. The deterministic C++17 checker enumerates every nonzero mask for each period 1..22 and every lag class, checks compatibility, exact primitivity, table rotation class, expected zero-ended multiplicity and the original modular-square recurrence. The resulting eight rows each form a unique orbit; all other cases fail. An independently structured direct ternary-word checker corroborates periods 1..11. No infinite claims rely on finite enumeration.

value.rationale: The 2026 paper highlights the arithmetic complexity of the nonlinear recurrence and gives specific seed periods 4,9,19,22. Classifying all primitive cycles for arbitrary initial states and all delay congruences through the fourth attainable length gives an exact small-cycle spectrum, excludes 5..8,10..18,20..21, and establishes uniqueness of each short phase orbit. This is a natural finite classification at the source-motivated frontier, not a single isolated instance, and supplies structural constraints for future period and basin studies.
